q: How do I calculate the carbon footprint of a piece of bamboo furniture?
title: Bamboo furniture carbon footprint per piece
short: Raw bamboo is a fast growing grass. Much of the footprint usually comes from treatment, drying, adhesives, finishes and any engineered board. Add those per piece and divide the workshop's energy by pieces made.
audience: Bamboo and cane furniture makers in the North East and Kerala

ul: Bamboo poles, splits or engineered bamboo board.
Treatment and drying, sometimes in a kiln.
Cutting, bending with heat and joining.

p: Report per piece by type and weight. Engineered bamboo board adds glue and pressing energy that raw poles do not.

example.title: Worked example: bamboo furniture unit per piece (one month)
lines: Plant total: 2,016 / 600 = 3.360 kg CO2 per piece
Add bamboo, adhesives and finishes for the full figure
example.note: Inputs are illustrative; use your own bills and production records.

senseible: Senseible reads the plant's electricity bills (CEA grid factor 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh for FY 2024-25, CO2 Baseline Database version 21.0) and fuel invoices (IPCC 2006 defaults) into a fingerprinted Scope 1 and 2 record, the plant-level input to a per-unit figure. Bought-in materials go to the supplier evidence trail; product reports are self-declared drafts.
